At the cash register, Shure reminded me to scan the membership code; lacking it, we explored alternatives including using the "88 membership" and coupons via the Hema app. Lucia clarified that the app was necessary for checkout, which was new information to me. We coordinated scanning multiple trolleys and waited for bill settlement. I opened Alipay on my phone, confirmed its usage with Shure, and handed over my phone for payment. The group briefly discussed privacy concerns regarding app permissions and data recording, agreeing to review these issues later. After payment, Tasha scanned the screen, and Shure returned my phone as product barcode scanning and packing proceeded, including checking device power and readiness.

I prepared charging equipment and assisted Tasha in connecting her headset to a power bank, ensuring all connections were secure. During checkout, I coordinated payment details, scanned coupons, and monitored product scanning alongside the group. I managed bill handling and proposed organization strategies for scanned and unscanned items. The group agreed on packing solutions and managing multiple shopping bags, with discussions clarifying scanning completion, coupon usage, and addressing copyright restrictions related to recording devices.

To handle heavy groceries, I assisted in carrying and loading bags into carts, following Tasha’s advice on providing delicate support. I proposed splitting the load into two carts, which Tasha and Alice supported, resolving transport challenges. After organizing bags into the new carts, I returned the initial cart and rearranged items for easier handling. We discussed renting additional carts and bag options, confirming plans to manage the load effectively before departure.

At the service desk, I inquired about cart rental but received no clear answer, so I informed Tasha that the plan was unworkable. We discussed the status of camera equipment and bag availability, clarifying payment for certain items. As preparations for a hotpot meal commenced, Tasha questioned the price of a kitchen wipe, leading me to retract that item. A debate followed regarding the identification of a vegetable as either green onion or garlic; I agreed to purchase additional green onions and managed bill handling despite some confusion over receipts, concluding with consensus to order green onions.

I examined bills with Katrina, Lucia, and others, confirming pricing and item details. I instructed the team to affix access controls on packages and coordinated sealing of fragile items. The group discussed potential incidents of item snatching and reviewed all bills comprehensively. I accepted assistance to affix bills and confirmed cart return directions with Shure, completing logistical management efficiently.

Following shopping completion, I returned the cart and participated in discussions about transporting and storing groceries. Shure planned to start the car; we debated dining options and agreed to go home first to better manage perishable items. At home, Shure directed checking refrigeration requirements. I assisted with bag handling on the floor while group members expressed concern over fridge capacity. I emphasized the importance of data management for traceability of stored items. Lucia compared our system to Amazon’s cashier-less stores, explaining automated tracking and occasional errors, which we observed and tested with the technology.

We prepared to move through a building, navigating with phone maps and elevator use while carrying items. Alice directed the route, and Shure accompanied us to the door. The group discussed vegetables, planned subway rides, and agreed to briefly record data. I coordinated with Shure and Tasha regarding inviting others to participate in the dataset, noting privacy sensitivities.

I placed bags down and made calls while checking maps. Shure offered a ride before the group parted ways. After confirming directions and following Alice’s navigation, I exited at the original entrance, thanked the group, and confirmed access for an expected visitor. While waiting, I conversed briefly about Singapore’s climate, explaining temperature ranges and my adaptation strategy of avoiding midday outdoor activity.

Using Alice’s phone, I checked our location and confirmed with the group that we were near Line 1 of the subway by recognizing landmarks such as Yonghe King and a taxi with hazard lights. Noting that my phone lacked credit for calls, I coordinated with Alice and others to verify our position. We decided to walk across the road toward the taxi together. While moving, I carried bags alongside Tasha and Katrina, assisted in opening the taxi trunk despite some head pain, and directed where to place the items. I declined additional help as Tasha closed the trunk. This event involved leading group navigation and managing luggage handling amidst minor physical discomfort.

The group boarded the bus and arranged seating to avoid suspicion and discomfort. Alice gave me her phone, which I advised not to use to prevent drawing attention, and then I returned my own phone. We agreed to sit in the back, with Katrina taking the boss’s seat and Lucia the front seat if no one became carsick. As the bus moved, I adjusted my bag and expressed physical discomfort. When Alice inquired about recording, I immediately turned off the GoPro, deciding it was unnecessary for this segment. Seating and recording arrangements were finalized to maintain group comfort and discretion during the ride.

I checked my phone’s timer and showed it to Tasha and others in the back seat to confirm timing. After confirming that Lucia had started, the group coordinated their observation from the back, with Alice and others commenting on the event’s progress. This established synchronized timing and attention among the group.

Upon the car stopping and the timer starting, I exited first with Katrina, Tasha, and Alice. We opened the trunk and began unloading a large volume of luggage and supplies. I organized heavier items despite comments on their weight, while Alice and others assisted in carrying and tidying spilled goods, including unexpected items not belonging to us. After loading was complete and the trunk closed, we left the car and headed toward an intersection as the sky darkened.

While walking away, the group discussed business class dress code and flowers observed nearby. At the intersection, after Tasha pointed out a path, I chose a narrow alley as our route home. We proceeded together carrying heavy supplies, discussing posters and directions while noting uncertainty about which house was ours. I reminded the group to stay focused during navigation and managed the heavy load despite its difficulty.

I carried water bags and initiated one-for-one item exchanges with Lucia, Alice, and Tasha to balance loads. Lucia and Alice lifted lighter items while I managed heavier ones. After realizing I had taken a wrong path, I turned back, handed an item to Alice, and we resumed walking together. Brief conversation touched on gym habits and challenges accessing gyms farther away.

Proceeding along a wider tree-lined road with electric bikes, we discussed placing a Xiaomi oven into a large bag per Tasha’s suggestion. Turning right into a small alley, I continued carrying heavy items past houses and fences, eventually reaching a door.

Lucia and I discussed the password, with others recalling it or suggesting we ask Xingrui. I retrieved the password from WeChat chat history on my phone and confirmed it to the group. Watching them enter the code, I guided the input until access was granted.

After entry, we collected items from the ground; Alice identified a fallen hat, which I placed in a plastic bag. We then walked into the yard, completing the organized transportation and entry process under password protection.
